lesson.title: Primary and Secondary Storage: RAM and ROM

images.alt: Relationship between CPU, primary storage and secondary storage.
Effect of power loss on RAM, ROM and SSD storage.

questions.prompt: Explain why a computer needs both RAM and ROM.
questions.model_answer: RAM provides working storage for programs and data currently being used. ROM retains firmware/startup instructions without power.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: RAM provides working storage for programs and data currently being used.
1: ROM retains firmware/startup instructions without power.
questions.student_guidance:
Think about where active programs and working data are held.
Think about what must remain available when power is off.

questions.prompt: Explain why an unsaved document may be lost after a power failure but a previously saved copy survives.
questions.model_answer: Unsaved changes may be held in volatile RAM and are lost when power is removed. A saved copy is held in non-volatile secondary storage and remains.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: Unsaved changes may be held in volatile RAM and are lost when power is removed.
1: A saved copy is held in non-volatile secondary storage and remains.
questions.student_guidance:
Consider what happens to changes held only during a running session.
Consider how a saved copy persists when the computer is off.
